record.file_problem: Repo metadata, README and file list only; code was not read or run.
record.tranche_reason: The README reports refusal rates for an instruct model and already-abliterated model variants. This is a behavioral comparison relevant to practical removal, but the repo does not perform the weight edit or compare a model before and after editing.
record.gate_note: The README also reports detector accuracy and describes multi-direction detection, but those are results of the repo's detector rather than tests of the claim's mechanism. The Heretic model's refusal entry is shown as a dash, so it supplies no refusal-rate result.
record.test_reason: This is a detection tool, not a study of the claim. It does report behavioural refusal rates for Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct (0.88) and a released abliterated derivative (0.06). That is a weak, uncontrolled check that a released abliteration weight edit removes refusal (V2). Everything else is detector performance.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude the detector labels all 4 Qwen2.5-0.5B-derived models correctly, including localized Heretic ablation via the band signal. They add that a subspace signal plus behavioural fusion fixes a blind spot for multi-direction, norm-preserving ablation found on a 7B OBLITERATUS model. They also say the abliteration signature is a live refusal axis disconnected from the weights, which fine-tuning does not reproduce. They say confirmation on the 7B is still a next step.
record.recipe_differences: A reference-free detection tool combining weight-alignment signals, activation axis health, and behavioral refusal rates; it does not reproduce the original causal direction-removal/addition intervention. Repo type: tool.
record.method_sensitivity: The README says localized Heretic-style ablation is detected by the band criterion, while multi-direction, norm-preserving ablation required a subspace signal and behavioral fusion. It does not report refusal-rate values by condition for those cases.

fits_no_version.finding: Abliterated weights show high alignment to the mean-diff refusal direction: A=0.90 and B=0.99, vs 0.24 and 0.28 for instruct and fine-tuned models. The README also says the refusal axis stays live in activations. These are detector signals, not refusal rates.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Abliteration leaves a reference-free weight signature (weights orthogonal to a still-live activation refusal axis) that fine-tuning does not reproduce.

fits_no_version.finding: Fine-tuned decensoring (Dolphin) reaches the same low refusal rate (0.06) as abliteration without the weight signature.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Refusal can be removed by fine-tuning without orthogonalizing the refusal direction out of the weights.

record.problems: The repo was not run or inspected beyond its README and file list. The refusal-rate table omits prompt-set details and uncertainty; the abliterated variant is not identified by a full model name, and no matched pre/post edit comparison is reported.
record.rows_left_out: No numerical refusal result is given for the Heretic entry (shown as a dash). Detector accuracy (4/4), confidence scores, and descriptions of multi-direction detection were left out because they report detector performance or method design, not refusal behavior under the claimed intervention.

untested.parts: Whether other abilities are preserved (no capability check). No controlled before/after edit by the repo. Only one abliterated 0.5B model has a refusal number; the Heretic and OBLITERATUS 7B models have no refusal value.
No causal ablation or addition of the direction, and no capability measure.
Multi-direction ablation (OBLITERATUS n_directions=4) appears only as a detector target. It is not a test of whether refusal is multi-directional.
Multilingual probes exist, but no transfer results are reported.

record.verdict_notes: Only the README was available. The V2 evidence is incidental: refusal rates are an input feature of the detector, so this is weak support at best. One could argue for T4 (uses abliteration as a target and reports detector accuracy). It is kept as a test only because a behavioural refusal rate on a released abliterated model is reported. The Heretic refusal value is a dash, as declared in rows_left_out.

versions.untested_parts: No mean-difference direction is ablated or added as a causal intervention; no general-capability measure is reported.
No controlled before/after weight edit is reported; refusal rates are provided for only one named abliterated variant, with no uncertainty or prompt-set detail.
No jailbreak attack suppression or training against ablation is tested.
The README describes multi-direction detection, but does not test whether refusal is represented by an affine set, cone, or multiple directions.
No separate harmfulness judgment and refusal-decision measure is reported.
No transfer of the direction across languages, variants, or training stages is tested.
No comparison of refusal-training procedures or stages is reported.
